result:
The proposed answer of N is very likely wrong. The reasoning assumes each of the N algebraic solitons contributes exactly one simple pole with a fixed imaginary part. That is not justified. An embedded eigenvalue of multiplicity N makes the double-Wronskian tau-function's polynomial structure more intricate than N independent single-pole contributions. From my recollection of the literature on rational solutions of the massive Thirring model, the N-th solution has N(N+1)/2 poles in the upper half x-plane for large |t|, which is a triangular number. I have not verified this against the source paper, so my confidence is moderate.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 3
